description: Arpeggiator taking a polyphonic chord and playing its notes one at a time in a chosen pattern, with programme, octave and modify settings per step

params.text: Sets how many of the programme, octave and modify rows are used, from 1 to 8
Picks the arpeggiation pattern: forward, reverse, pendulum, random, middle-out, outside-in, skip-and-back, or P to follow the programme buttons
Sorts the incoming notes low to high or high to low, or leaves them in the order they arrive, before the pattern is applied
Sets the glide time given to a note whose modify row has glide switched on, up to half a second
Turns the octave row on, so each step can shift its note an octave up or down
Turns the modify row on, so each step can switch on glide or accent
Locks the arpeggiator onto the chord that is playing, so changes at the V/OCT and GATE inputs are ignored; every other control keeps working

inputs.text: The gates for the incoming chord, read at the start of each clock pulse; the number of channels here sets how many notes are arpeggiated
The chord to arpeggiate, one note per channel at a volt per octave, read at the start of each clock pulse
Each pulse moves the arpeggio on to the next note
A trigger here restarts the pattern at its first note
A high gate here locks the arpeggiator onto the chord that is playing, and while a cable is patched the HOLD button follows this input

outputs.text: Goes high for the note being played, and stays low on a step programmed as a rest
The pitch of the note being played, at a volt per octave
A 10V gate on any note whose modify row has accent switched on

notes: a gate at GATE is what plays each note; with nothing patched there the arpeggiator plays nothing, whatever is at V/OCT
a PROGRAMME button responds to a click only while SEQUENCE is set to P, an OCTAVE button only while OCT is on and a MODIFY button only while MOD is on
a button on a row past the LENGTH setting does nothing, and clicking a lit PROGRAMME or OCTAVE button puts that step back to its default
the programme, octave and modify rows run independently of the notes, so setting a row length that differs from the number of notes phases the two against each other
menu: Polyphonic Outputs — sends each note out on its own channel rather than one at a time
Monophonic gate input — takes the number of notes from the V/OCT input, so that one gate can drive a whole chord

inputs.2: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.3: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.4: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
